content:
The [JavaScript Minifier/Beautifier](/javascript-minifier-beautifier) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Minify JavaScript to shrink it, or beautify it back into readable code. Enter your javaScript code and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Minify JavaScript to make it smaller for production, or beautify minified code back into readable, indented JavaScript. The minifier strips comments and unneeded whitespace while keeping the code's meaning — it understands strings, template literals, regular expressions and the places where a newline matters, so minified code still runs exactly like the original. The beautifier re-indents code with two-space indentation. Everything runs in your browser; your code is never uploaded. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the JavaScript Minifier/Beautifier

Start by typing or pasting your javaScript code. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults. The steps below walk through each input in order.

1. Paste your JavaScript into the editor (or use the sample).
2. Choose Minify to shrink it or Beautify to re-format it, then copy the result.
3. Check the byte count and saving shown under the output.

## How it works

The [JavaScript Minifier/Beautifier](/javascript-minifier-beautifier) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result.

Here is a typical example. Minifying a 200-byte function with comments removes the comments and extra spaces, typically saving 20–40%. Beautifying the result restores the indentation and line breaks. Try the same figures in the [JavaScript Minifier/Beautifier](/javascript-minifier-beautifier) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## Trying it out

The fastest way to see what the [JavaScript Minifier/Beautifier](/javascript-minifier-beautifier) does is to open it and enter values you already know the answer for. Change one input at a time and watch how the result responds — that tells you more than any description. Everything runs in your browser, so you can experiment freely: nothing is saved, sent or tracked.

## What the minifier keeps intact

Strings, template literals (including ${...} expressions), regular expressions and the newlines that JavaScript's automatic semicolon insertion depends on — for example after return. Minified code is safe to run as-is, but always test minified code before shipping it, as with any build step.

## What it is not

This is a straightforward minifier, not a full bundler or obfuscator: it does not rename variables, remove dead code or bundle modules. For a production build pipeline, a bundler such as esbuild, Rollup or webpack is still the right tool. This one is for quick one-off jobs and for reading minified code.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Minify a copy, not your only copy — keep the readable source safe.
- Test minified code before deploying it, especially if it uses unusual syntax.
- Use Beautify to read a minified file someone else sent you.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### What does a JavaScript minifier do?

It removes comments and unnecessary whitespace from JavaScript so the file is smaller and loads faster, without changing what the code does. Try it with your own numbers in the [JavaScript Minifier/Beautifier](/javascript-minifier-beautifier) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Is my code uploaded anywhere?

No. The minifier and beautifier run entirely in your browser. Your code never leaves your device. Try it with your own numbers in the [JavaScript Minifier/Beautifier](/javascript-minifier-beautifier) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Will minified code still work?

Yes — the minifier preserves strings, template literals, regular expressions and the line breaks that matter for automatic semicolon insertion. As with any build step, test the result before shipping. Try it with your own numbers in the [JavaScript Minifier/Beautifier](/javascript-minifier-beautifier) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What is the difference between minify and beautify?

Minify shrinks code for production; beautify does the opposite, re-indenting compressed code so a human can read it again. Try it with your own numbers in the [JavaScript Minifier/Beautifier](/javascript-minifier-beautifier) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.
